correctness.rationale: The original weighted mathematics is correct: at high-set mass t the two-block quadratic form has trace 2−t and determinant (1−t)². Its positive top eigenvector realizes the high/low ratio in the Finding, and equality in the blockwise Cauchy–Schwarz inequalities enforces constancy on both blocks. In the repaired question only the universal-bound equality is needed: det((4/3)I−B(t))=(t−1/3)² and the lower diagonal entry is positive, so equality requires t=1/3, and the values 4 and 1 are an exact witness. A nonzero maximizer exists by finite-dimensional compactness. In the reduction the masses sum to 3L; the last mass exceeds L, and the original masses alone total less than L, so the subset must include L−T and the original target is exactly T. Descending subset-sum updates and the subset certificate give the claimed weak NP-completeness and decision bound.
residual_risks: The finite checks are not an exhaustion of all integer inputs or real masses; the analytic and complexity proofs are decisive. The repaired question concerns exact equality, not approximation.

evidence: Before maximizing over k, §3.1 proves the bound with squared coefficient Φ(k/n) for a fixed active set. The two block constants and their ratio follow from equality in (3.1) and (3.2).

The same-day weighted-star record's limit as hub mass tends to zero is max Φ(k/q) on q equal-mass leaves. This verifies an exact shared analytical specialization, not the binary-input complexity assertion.
broader_coverage.reasoning: For integer masses clone each atom to its mass in indistinguishable counting-measure vertices. Rational masses follow by rescaling, and the same two-block inequality holds for arbitrary positive reals by replacing the within-block sums with mass-weighted ones; the equality conditions are unchanged. The analytically broad coverage supplies the criterion but does not prove a reduction polynomial in the compressed mass encoding.

evidence: The conditional expectations of |f| onto the trivial and full atomic sigma algebras are its weighted mean and |f| itself, so the two-time Doob maximal operator on this filtration is identical after probability normalization.
The norm hits the universal bound exactly when whole atoms of total probability 1/3 can be selected, not when arbitrary fractions of atoms can be selected.

The inspected mathematical and indexed coverage did not establish the complexity of this specific norm-equality problem. This is not a pass for the original analytical headline or a claim of exhaustive priority.

value.rationale: The repaired statement answers whether one can recognize saturation of the sharp bound efficiently from the natural compact mass representation. The graph geometry is fixed by the number of atoms, yet equality detection distinguishes a trivial cardinality test from a weakly NP-complete arithmetic obstruction. The encoding distinction and pseudo-polynomial boundary are useful independently of claiming a new norm formula.
residual_risks: The hard problem is sharp-bound attainment, not approximate evaluation or strong NP-hardness; no broader complexity claim is inferred.
